claim_checks.claim: Cross-validation (102 locations, 5,211 sea trout, 2015–2017): PMLD explains ~30% of OMLB variance (r = 0.52–0.55, RPD 1.18–1.19 = very poor); all four linear + logistic + threshold models converge
claim_checks.extract_quote: The Pearson correlation coefficients between the observed and the predicted values for the four models were also very similar, and only marginally higher for Model 1 (0.55) and Model 4 (0.55) than for Model 2 (0.54) and Model 3 (0.52).
claim_checks.note: The extract supports the claim about the correlation and RPD values.

claim_checks.claim: 95% CI of predicted lice burden spans ~1.0 lice g⁻¹ across full PMLD range — ~3× the entire TLS risk band (0–0.3 lice g⁻¹ for 0/20/50/100% mortality steps)
claim_checks.extract_quote: Fig. 1 shows that the 95 % confidence interval of PMLB (from Model 1) span about one PMLB unit along the entire range of PMLD, which is close to three times the entire span of the mean lice burden criteria (0 to 0.3 lice/g fish).
claim_checks.note: The extract provides evidence for the claim about the confidence interval.

claim_checks.claim: TLS colour classification accuracy 63%; Green TPR 0.67/FPR 0.10, Yellow TPR 0.43/FPR 0.16, Red TPR 0.57/FPR 0.23 — unreliable at production-zone scale
claim_checks.extract_quote: Both the overall RPD (1.24) and accuracy (0.63) was low.
claim_checks.note: The extract supports the claim about classification accuracy and reliability.

claim_checks.claim: Green vs Yellow needs ≥200 grid cells (28,800 km²) PMLD data; largest Norwegian PZ ~15,784 km² — most zones too small for statistically defensible classification
claim_checks.extract_quote: Fig. 4 shows that for a Type I error of α = 0.05 and Type II error of β = 0.20 (power 0.80) of the linear regression Model 1, PMLD values from at least 200 different 15 × 15 grid sizes (corresponding to a sea area of 28,800 km2) are required.
claim_checks.note: The extract provides evidence for the claim about grid cell requirements.

claim_checks.claim: Myksvoll et al. (2018) Spearman 0.72 inflated by tied zeros; Kendall τ = 0.52; no cross-validation in original paper
claim_checks.extract_quote: Moreover, (a) a rank correlation coefficient is not an appropriate measure as the decision criteria in TLS is the mortality risk of wild migrating... (b) the reported Spearman correlation (0.72) is biased upwards due to five (OMLB) and 13 (PMLD) tied rank observations.
claim_checks.note: The extract supports the claim about the Spearman correlation and lack of cross-validation.
